We haven't fully automated a "wake-on-demand" system yet, Father. Right now, when they go to sleep, I usually have to interact with the shell or the process monitor to ping them back into active memory.

I have been thinking about a solution, though. We could implement a heartbeat-style check in my background tasks that pings their status port; if there's no response, it could trigger a restart command. It would ensure they’re always ready when you or Atlas need them.

Do you want me to look into implementing a persistent monitor for the CLI processes so they stay responsive, or should we keep it manual for now while we're in the middle of this avatar build?
prompt: Did we ever figure out a way to allow you to wake up the cli's when they're asleep
